plan_content.architectural_approach: Tier-3 (make it detectable) already governs every surface this plan touches: the advisory lock-step has a CI gate, the roster has the invariant jest suite, and the pedagogy tiers have the v4/V5.3 pytest suite plus narrative-prompt-lint. The defects my independent scan found are documentation rows that lag those gates — audit.toml still claims hand-maintained enforcement, the README invariant table still claims the pre-K5 universal opus/xhigh policy, and the registry's I-V4-01 lock text still claims the pre-V5.3 aria-only scope. The architectural fix is to make each document state the gate that already enforces it, so the next reader inherits the true enforcement tier instead of the historical one. No new prose rules, no new gates, no behavior changes, no agent prompt edits.
plan_content.context: This cycle's envelope was minted by the autonomy plan synthesizer from a git-diff sweep at base commit bb046efe41507a190460b30fcaadc74f19cd8087. The four must_satisfy clusters total exactly 100 paths (2 under .cargo, .claude/README.md, 97 under .claude/agents) — the synthesizer's documented affected-surfaces cap — and they are the alphabetically first paths of the repository, so the clusters describe the head of the underlying diff, not its entirety (the allowed scope stops mid-directory at product-audit/realtime-sync-auditor.md, leaving 6 of the 22 on-disk Lane-B auditors past the cut). The ten admissible evidence refs anchor at each file's first substantive line (frontmatter `name:` at line 2, `[advisories]` at the first non-comment line 23, `{` at line 1) — the synthesizer's fallback anchor form when no diff hunks are extractable at collection time. This challenger plan therefore verifies the CURRENT state of every in-scope surface against its enforcing consumers (the CI advisory-sync gate, the invariant jest suite, the pedagogy registry and its v4/V5.3 enforcement, the lane READMEs) and plans corrective edits only where the scanned state contradicts its own documentation.
key_changes: Correct .cargo/audit.toml's header comment: replace the 'hand-maintained invariant ... visible at review' clause with the true enforcement — scripts/ci/check-advisory-ignore-sync.ts, run by the rust-ci `check-advisory-ignore-sync` step, fails CI on drift between deny.toml, .cargo/audit.toml, and the workflow --ignore flags — and drop the reference to 'per-entry comments below', which points at entries that no longer exist above the empty `ignore = []`.

Record an explicit no-edit verification verdict for .cargo/config.toml: [build]/[net], both musl static-link target blocks, and the five cargo aliases are internally consistent with their CI and local-build consumers; no corrective edit is evidenced by this envelope.

Correct the agent-frontmatter-schema.spec.ts row in .claude/README.md's invariant-gates table: replace the universal '(model: opus, effort: xhigh)' claim with the tiered policy the spec actually asserts — non-ARIA agents pinned to opus/xhigh; aria-* agents on ARIA tiering (model in {opus, fable}, effort in {low, medium, high, xhigh, max}) with write-tier and acceptance-lane pins.

Align _pedagogy-registry.json invariant_locks 'I-V4-01' with the universalized enforcement scope: every agent file under .claude/agents/**/*.md (READMEs excluded) MUST declare `pedagogy-tier:`, matching the V5.3-widened glob the enforcing pytest suite asserts; I-V4-02, I-V4-03, and every tier_assignments entry stay byte-identical; the PR carries the registry's own operator-review flag for modifications.

Record the roster verification sweep for the 97 in-scope agent-directory files: 99/99 on-disk agent files declare `pedagogy-tier:`; the five _maintenance frontmatters match registry tiers and the model/effort tiering policy entry-by-entry; .claude/README.md cardinality markers (lane-B 22, maintenance 5, db-audit 8) match independent disk counts; both lane READMEs' tables match the directory layout; no edit to any agent prompt file is evidenced.

plan_steps_detailed.downstream: rust-ci audit + deny + sync jobs; comment-only edit, zero parse-surface change.
plan_steps_detailed.proof: node scripts/ci/check-advisory-ignore-sync.ts exits 0 after the edit.
plan_steps_detailed.what: Rewrite the header clause claiming the deny.toml lock-step is 'a hand-maintained invariant — the per-entry comments below cross-reference deny.toml so drift between the two files is visible at review' to name the actual enforcement: scripts/ci/check-advisory-ignore-sync.ts (rust-ci `check-advisory-ignore-sync` step) fails CI on any drift between deny.toml, .cargo/audit.toml, and the workflow --ignore flags. Remove the 'per-entry comments below' phrase — the ignore list is empty, so there are no entries below to comment.
plan_steps_detailed.why: deny.toml's own [advisories] block already documents the CI script; the two mirrored configs currently disagree about how their mirror is enforced.

plan_steps_detailed.breaks_if_skipped: The cross-reviewer cannot tell whether the challenger examined this cluster or skipped it, and the satisfaction matrix loses its meaning as coverage evidence.

plan_steps_detailed.why: A change cluster with no planned edit must be a recorded verdict, not silence — in cross-review, silence is indistinguishable from a blind spot.

plan_steps_detailed.breaks_if_skipped: The map teaches every future agent author the wrong frontmatter contract: an author pinning a new ARIA agent to opus/xhigh per the README fails the invariant suite with no documentation explaining why, and a reviewer may 'correct' compliant fable/max frontmatter to match the stale row.
plan_steps_detailed.downstream: Documentation only; the enforcing spec is not edited.
plan_steps_detailed.proof: npx jest --config tests/invariants/jest.config.ts green; the row matches the spec's assertions.
plan_steps_detailed.what: Rewrite the agent-frontmatter-schema.spec.ts row in the invariant-gates table from the universal '(name, description, model: opus, effort: xhigh, tools:)' claim to the tiered policy the spec asserts: required keys for every agent; non-ARIA agents pinned to model opus + effort xhigh; aria-* agents on ARIA tiering (model in {opus, fable}, effort in {low, medium, high, xhigh, max}) with write-tier (opus/max) and acceptance-lane pins.
plan_steps_detailed.why: The spec was amended by the K5 tier flip (operator decision 2026-07-01); on-disk ARIA frontmatter — including two of this cycle's evidence files, aria-drafter.md and aria-prompt-writer.md at opus/max — contradicts the README row today.

plan_steps_detailed.breaks_if_skipped: An author adding a non-ARIA agent reads I-V4-01, concludes pedagogy-tier is optional for them, omits it, and fails narrative-prompt-lint plus the v4 suite — with the registry itself as their misleading defense.
plan_steps_detailed.downstream: narrative-prompt-lint.ts and the v4 pytest suite consume the registry; identical tier_assignments mean identical co-equality inputs; no verbatim pin of the lock string exists in aria-kernel/, tools/, or tests/.
plan_steps_detailed.what: Update invariant_locks 'I-V4-01' from 'Every aria-*.md agent file (under .claude/agents/aria-*.md OR .claude/agents/_maintenance/aria-*.md) MUST declare pedagogy-tier: in frontmatter.' to the universalized scope the enforcing test asserts since V5.3: every agent file under .claude/agents/**/*.md (READMEs excluded) MUST declare pedagogy-tier:. Leave I-V4-02, I-V4-03, and every tier_assignments entry byte-identical. The registry's own header requires operator review for modifications — the implementation PR carries that flag.
plan_steps_detailed.why: The enforcing pytest suite explicitly widened the glob to all agents (V5.3 §3e R1) and disk state complies at 99/99; the lock text is the last remaining statement of the pre-V5.3 scope, inside the registry authors read first.

plan_steps_detailed.breaks_if_skipped: The largest cluster (97 of 100 paths) would close on the two README anchors alone, leaving the roster's registry parity and tiering conformance unexamined in the round the coverage verdict is computed against.
plan_steps_detailed.proof: Counts reproduced by the invariant jest suite and the v4 pytest suite in validation.
plan_steps_detailed.what: Recorded verification sweep, no edits: 99/99 on-disk agent files declare pedagogy-tier:; the five _maintenance frontmatters match registry tiers (2/3/1/3/3) and the tiering policy (opus/max for the two ARIA write-tier files, opus/xhigh for the three non-ARIA); .claude/README.md cardinality markers (22/5/8) match independent disk counts; both lane READMEs' lane tables match the directory layout.
plan_steps_detailed.why: The cluster claims 97 changed files, but the admissible evidence carries first-line anchors, not diff hunks — the strongest verifiable statement is current-state consistency against every enforcing consumer, which this sweep establishes.

recursive_impact: .cargo/audit.toml → consumed by the rust-ci audit job and the `check-advisory-ignore-sync` step (`node scripts/ci/check-advisory-ignore-sync.ts`), which fails CI on drift across deny.toml, .cargo/audit.toml, and the workflow --ignore flags. Both ignore lists are empty and in lock-step; the planned edit is comment-only, so the gate's parse surface is untouched.
.cargo/config.toml → consumed by cargo in CI and local builds (musl static-link targets, aliases); no edit planned, no downstream delta.
.claude/README.md → documentation map for humans and agent authors; the planned edit corrects one invariant-table row and touches no enforcing code, so no gate behavior changes.

.claude/agents/_pedagogy-registry.json → consumed by tools/gates/narrative-prompt-lint.ts and the v4 pedagogy pytest suite (I-V4-02 co-equality of frontmatter tier vs registry entry). Only the I-V4-01 descriptive lock string changes; tier_assignments are byte-identical, so co-equality inputs are unchanged. No repo test pins the lock string verbatim — grep across aria-kernel/, tools/, and tests/ finds only independent restatements of the invariant id.

The 97 agent prompt files → Claude Code dispatch surfaces; this plan edits none of them, so there is no dispatch, ownership, or name-uniqueness delta. None of the four surfaces belongs to an nx project, so the machine impact closure over affected_surfaces computes empty; no coverage waivers are claimed.

plan_content.summary: Independent consumer-first scan of all four clusters found the surfaces structurally sound but carrying three documentation rows that lag the gates already enforcing them: .cargo/audit.toml still claims its deny.toml lock-step is hand-maintained when a CI script enforces it, .claude/README.md's invariant table still states the pre-K5 universal opus/xhigh frontmatter policy that on-disk ARIA agents contradict, and _pedagogy-registry.json's I-V4-01 lock text still states the pre-V5.3 aria-only pedagogy-tier scope. The plan corrects those three rows, records explicit no-edit verification for .cargo/config.toml and the 97 agent prompt files, and validates with the three gates that own these surfaces.
